hero.quote: "Nicknamed 'Halong Bay on Land', this 54-hole mega-resort offers a surreal golfing experience amidst towering limestone karst mountains in North Vietnam."

overviewParagraphs: Set in a landscape that seems straight out of a fantasy movie, Phoenix Golf Resort offers a golfing experience unlike any other. The towering limestone formations provide a dramatic and intimidating backdrop to almost every shot across the 54-hole complex. The three courses offer varied challenges: the Phoenix Course (designed by Ron Fream), the Dragon Course (by Japanese designer Tatsukawa), and the Master Course (by Calvin Peete). Each course demands accuracy to avoid the water hazards, deep rough, and out-of-bounds areas created by the natural rocky terrain. The resort's massive European-style clubhouse stands as a grand centerpiece, offering extensive facilities, locker rooms, and dining options to accommodate hundreds of golfers daily.

curatorBriefHtml: Phoenix Golf Resort in Hoa Binh Province (about 60 minutes southwest of central Hanoi) is Vietnam’s largest golf complex — a sprawling 54-hole destination nick-named "Ha Long Bay on Land" for the dramatic limestone karst spires rising directly behind its fairways. Three distinct 18-hole layouts — the Dragon Course, Champion Course, and Phoenix Course (7,184 yards, Par 72) — were crafted by Ron Fream, Calvin Peete, and Japanese/Korean design teams.

While Phoenix’s conditioning is more traditional resort-grade than Hanoi’s ultra-modern private clubs like Sky Lake or Thanh Lanh, its limestone-cliff scenery is genuinely jaw-dropping and its 54-hole capacity makes it a dependable option for larger 16- to 32-golfer corporate or society groups needing simultaneous morning tee times.
AGS recommends requesting the Dragon Course for the most dramatic karst vistas and tightest mountain corridors, pairing Phoenix with Sky Lake or BRG Kings Island on a Hanoi golf week.

scorecard.verdict: Dubbed 'Ha Long Bay on Land,' the 54-hole Phoenix Golf Resort delivers jaw-dropping scenery as you play between towering vertical limestone pillars rising from the valley floor.

faqs.q: Which of the three 18-hole courses at Phoenix Golf Resort is best?
faqs.a: The Dragon Course offers the most dramatic limestone karst scenery and tighter mountain shotmaking, while the Champion Course plays slightly wider and more forgiving for mixed-handicap touring groups.

faqs.q: How far is Phoenix Golf Resort from central Hanoi?
faqs.a: Phoenix lies in Luong Son (Hoa Binh Province), approximately 55 to 70 minutes southwest of central Hanoi by private touring vehicle.

faqs.q: Why is Phoenix Golf Resort called 'Ha Long Bay on Land'?
faqs.a: Towering vertical limestone karst formations encircle the valley and sit directly behind several green complexes, mirroring the geological drama of Ha Long Bay.

faqs.q: What is the best time of year to play Phoenix Golf Resort?
faqs.a: October through April brings cool, clear Northern Vietnam weather (18–26°C) when mountain visibility is sharpest.
